items.text: Whether machines could ever truly feel is still wide open, and everything about their moral status and our own self-understanding hangs on the answer.
Before any structural case can be made, the pull toward seeing minds in machines has to be named as bias rather than evidence.
With the psychological seduction diagnosed, the harder work of testing computational functionalism itself replaces mere suspicion with argument.
Having made real machine consciousness look unlikely but not impossible, the question shifts from what AI is to how we should act under that remaining uncertainty.
Settled: intelligence and consciousness come apart, and computation alone probably cannot manufacture the latter; left open: what, short of mimicking us, would actually count as a soul in silicon.
